description: Connectivity between the sites and segments, and how much traffic flows between each pair of network segments. Connectivity comes from internet-probe LAN targets; segment pairs come from NetFlow on the OPNsense firewall (segflows).

panels.description: Source: internet_probe_lan_up from internet-probe on each site's host. 0 when a round failed in the last 15 s, lowest value in each interval so a short outage is not averaged away. A target that refuses the connection counts as up (something answered). One lane per site and target, so the same name is probed from several vantage points: opnsense-lan from homelab, the ER605 from home and homelab and blr. Gaps mean the probe host was off.
panels.title: LAN targets up or down

panels.description: Source: internet_probe_lan_down_seconds_total and internet_probe_lan_outages_total, increase over the range, per site and target name. Availability is 1 - downtime / range from confirmed outages only (the same confirm-rounds rule as the internet outages), so a single failed round is a blip and does not count. Capped by Prometheus retention (7 days); the probe host's ledger keeps every LAN outage (internet-probe.py --report lan).
panels.title: LAN availability and outages in range

panels.description: Source: internet_probe_lan_rtt_seconds, the TCP connect time of the last round, per site and target. Omitted while a target is failing, so a gap here with a red lane above is a down target, not a missing exporter.
panels.title: LAN round-trip time per target

panels.description: Source: the internet-probe journal lines in Loki (30 days), one per closed LAN outage (lan_up), filtered by the selected sites. Fields are the labels that | logfmt extracts from the line. closed_by=restart means the poller restarted during the outage, so the end is the restart time. Outages still open are not here; the lane above shows them. Older history: internet-probe.py --report lan on the host.
panels.title: LAN outages (30 days, Loki)

panels.description: Source: opnsense_segflow_bytes_total, increase over the range, per source and destination segment (NetFlow on the firewall, counted once per flow; see Coverage for which interfaces it sees). Direction matters: TENANT to INTERNET is upload, INTERNET to TENANT is download. Traffic inside one segment never reaches the firewall and is not counted. Capped by Prometheus retention (7 days); the firewall's ledger keeps it for good (segflows.py --report pairs).
panels.title: Bytes between segments, in range

panels.description: Source: opnsense_segflow_{bytes,packets,flows}_total, increase over the range, per source and destination segment. Flows are NetFlow records, so a long connection is several. Sorted by bytes.
panels.title: Segment pairs table

panels.description: Source: opnsense_segflow_bytes_total, increase over the range, as a matrix: the row is the source segment, the column the destination. Empty cell means no flow crossed the firewall between that pair in the range, which includes pairs it cannot see. The diagonal is traffic that entered and left the firewall on the same segment (rare).
panels.title: Matrix: bytes from row to column, in range

panels.description: Source: opnsense_segflow_bytes_total, rate per source and destination segment in bits per second. The counters move once per 5-minute run, so the rate is flat between runs and the series is a five-minute average of what the firewall's NetFlow exporter reported. Pick pairs with the From and To pickers.
panels.title: Rate between segments

panels.description: Source: opnsense_interfaces_received_bytes_total (opnsense-exporter), rate per interface in bits per second: what the hosts on each segment sent into the firewall. These counters are the interface totals and see everything, unlike the NetFlow pair counters, which cover only the captured interfaces. Same-segment traffic is not included.
panels.title: Received per segment (sent into the firewall)

panels.description: Source: opnsense_interfaces_transmitted_bytes_total (opnsense-exporter), rate per interface in bits per second: what the firewall delivered to each segment. WAN is the link to the home LAN, which carries the internet-bound traffic too.
panels.title: Transmitted per segment (delivered by the firewall)

panels.description: Source: node_network_receive_bytes_total{device="tailscale0"} from each host's node_exporter, rate in bits per second. This is the inter-site link: traffic between Bangalore, home and the homelab rides the tailnet, direct or through a relay. Hosts without Tailscale have no series.
panels.title: Tailnet received per host

panels.description: Source: node_network_transmit_bytes_total{device="tailscale0"} from each host's node_exporter, rate in bits per second. Read together with the received panel: a host that sends here and whose peer receives is one transfer seen from both ends.
panels.title: Tailnet transmitted per host

panels.description: Source: opnsense_segflow_lag_seconds, now minus the receive time of the newest flow the collector processed. The collector deliberately leaves the last 10 s unread, and runs every 5 minutes, so a few minutes is normal. Red above 15 minutes: segflows.py has stopped, or flowd has stopped exporting.
panels.title: Collector lag

panels.description: Source: time() minus opnsense_segflow_last_run_timestamp_seconds, how long ago the cron job last finished a run. The job runs every 5 minutes: red above 15 minutes. No data means the textfile is missing, so the job was never installed or node_exporter is not scraped.
panels.title: Last run

panels.description: Source: opnsense_segflow_run_duration_seconds, how long the last run took. It reads up to a day of flowd history on the first run and only the new five minutes after that.
panels.title: Run duration

panels.description: Source: opnsense_segflow_capture_interfaces, read from the firewall's netgraph netflow nodes (the interfaces ticked under Reporting > NetFlow). Only traffic that crosses one of these is counted in the pair panels. Anything not listed is not seen.
panels.title: Interfaces NetFlow captures

panels.description: Source: the interfaces the exporter reports (opnsense_interfaces_received_bytes_total) minus opnsense_segflow_capture_interfaces. Flows to or from a segment listed here are only counted when the other end is on a captured interface. Add the interface with netflow-capture.php (or under Reporting > NetFlow) to see them. WAN is never captured and is not listed. An empty table means every internal interface is captured.
panels.title: Segments NetFlow does not capture

panels.description: Explains what the pair panels cannot see. No query.

options.content:
### What this dashboard does not see

- **Traffic inside one segment or inside the home LAN switch.** Two hosts on the same VLAN talk through the switch and never reach the firewall, so no flow exists. Guest Traffic (the hypervisor's view) sees same-segment traffic between guests.
- **Interfaces NetFlow does not capture.** Only the interfaces listed in the Coverage row export flows. A flow between two uncaptured segments is invisible; one between a captured and an uncaptured segment is seen once, from the captured side.
- **Per-device home traffic.** The ER605 forwards in hardware; a per-device breakdown of the home network needs the planned port mirror of its LAN ports. Home appears here as one segment, HOME.
- **Traffic that is not a flow yet.** A connection is exported when it ends, goes idle (15 s) or hits the 30-minute active timeout, plus the 5-minute run interval, so the newest minutes are always missing.

panels.title: What is not measured

panels.description: Availability of each LAN target from each probe site. Source: PostgreSQL net_history (datasource Network history), rolled up hourly by net-history and kept forever; always the last 24 months, whatever the time picker says.

targets.rawSql: SELECT month::timestamp AS time, site || '/' || name AS metric, availability AS value FROM net.monthly_lan WHERE month >= (date_trunc('month', now() AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') - interval '23 months')::date ORDER BY 1

panels.title: LAN availability per target per month

panels.description: Confirmed LAN outages per probe site and target. Source: PostgreSQL net_history (datasource Network history), rolled up hourly by net-history and kept forever; always the last 24 months, whatever the time picker says.

targets.rawSql: SELECT month::timestamp AS time, site || '/' || name AS metric, outages AS value FROM net.monthly_lan WHERE month >= (date_trunc('month', now() AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') - interval '23 months')::date ORDER BY 1

panels.title: LAN outages per target per month

panels.description: NetFlow bytes from one segment to another. Source: PostgreSQL net_history (datasource Network history), rolled up hourly by net-history and kept forever; always the last 24 months, whatever the time picker says.

targets.rawSql: SELECT month::timestamp AS time, src_segment || ' > ' || dst_segment AS metric, bytes AS value FROM net.monthly_segflow WHERE month >= (date_trunc('month', now() AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') - interval '23 months')::date ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Bytes per segment pair per month

panels.description: Bytes routed per OPNsense segment (received plus transmitted). Source: PostgreSQL net_history (datasource Network history), rolled up hourly by net-history and kept forever; always the last 24 months, whatever the time picker says.

targets.rawSql: SELECT month::timestamp AS time, interface AS metric, total_bytes AS value FROM net.monthly_segment WHERE month >= (date_trunc('month', now() AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') - interval '23 months')::date ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Bytes per segment per month

panels.description: Bytes on tailscale0, received plus transmitted, per host. Source: PostgreSQL net_history (datasource Network history), rolled up hourly by net-history and kept forever; always the last 24 months, whatever the time picker says.

targets.rawSql: SELECT month::timestamp AS time, host AS metric, total_bytes AS value FROM net.monthly_tailnet WHERE month >= (date_trunc('month', now() AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') - interval '23 months')::date ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Tailnet per host per month

panels.description: Every closed LAN target outage, newest first (last 500). closed_by restart means the end is the poller restart time. Source: PostgreSQL net_history (datasource Network history), kept forever.

targets.rawSql: SELECT started_at AS "Start", ended_at AS "End", site AS "Site", kind AS "Kind", name AS "Name", target AS "Target", duration_seconds AS duration_seconds, cause AS "Cause", closed_by AS "Closed by" FROM net.outage_events WHERE kind IN ('lan') ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 500

panels.title: LAN outage history (permanent)

title: Inter-LAN
